source_text: In causa iudicandi, amoto strepitu turbarum, de omni ordine conversationis hominum, sive sacerdotum, sive administrantium, sive praefectorum, ad discussionem talium rerum non sola nomina, sed eligendam esse prudentiam, et honorandam esse paucitatem, quam ratio, eruditio, libertasque sublimat
pass_a_gloss: In case/cause iudicandi, having-been-removed noise of-crowds, about/from omni ordine of-conduct of-human-beings, or of-priests, or of-administrators, or of-governors, to discussionem such rerum not alone names, but eligendam to-be prudence, and honorandam to-be fewness, than/which reason, learning, freedom-and raises-up.
pass_b_english: When judging a case, the noise of the crowds must be put aside. From every walk of life—whether priests, administrators, or governors—we should choose wisdom, rather than mere titles, for the examination of such questions. We should honor the few whom reason, learning, and independence raise above the rest.
[He promises] to conduct this case against us, one man on behalf of everyone.
It brings me greater glory before God to defend truth when it has been abandoned.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
